title: Open restriction conjugates the canonical base-change stalk arrow
statement: Let $Y,B,A$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], $p:Y\to B$ a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism, $M$ an $\mathcal O_Y$-module sheaf, $g:A\to B$ a morphism, and $a\in A$. Let $S\subset B$ and $V\subset A$ be open subschemes with $a\in V$ and $V\subset g^{-1}(S)$. Put $p_S=p|_S$, $M_S=M|_{p^{-1}(S)}$, $j=g|_V:V\to S$, and $x_V=(a,a\in V)$. Let $F$ be the stalk functor at $x_V$ followed by restriction of scalars along the inverse $\mathcal O_{V,x_V}\simeq\mathcal O_{A,a}$. Write $b=\operatorname{standardSingleBaseChangeMap}(p,M,g)$ and $b_S=\operatorname{standardSingleBaseChangeMap}(p_S,M_S,j)$ [def-pc-standard-single-base-change-map]. For every $n\in\mathbf Z$ there are $\mathcal O_{A,a}$-linear isomorphisms $s:(H^n(\operatorname{source}(b)))_a\simeq F(H^n(\operatorname{source}(b_S)))$ and $t:F(H^n(\operatorname{target}(b_S)))\simeq(H^n(\operatorname{target}(b)))_a$. They satisfy $(H^n(b))_a=t\circ F(H^n(b_S))\circ s$. All derived categories are the standard localizations [def-pc-derived-category]; stalk functors are [def-pc-module-stalk-functor]. No flatness, quasi-coherence, affineness, or presentation is assumed.

proof.text: Use standardSingle_open_derived_arrow to obtain source and target isomorphisms of the restricted derived arrows and their commuting square. No geometric finiteness is used in this comparison.

Construct a natural linear restriction-stalk isomorphism for V inclusion into A. Mathlib restrictStalkNatIso gives the additive maps. On a common germ neighbourhood, germ_smul and the inverse stalk-map germ formula prove linearity after restriction of scalars. Its additive bijectivity gives a linear isomorphism, natural on all sheaf maps. overFunctorEquiv identifies the slice-site restriction with the literal restriction; Opens.stalkIso_inv identifies the scalar map with the one in F. Compose with mapDerivedCategoryHomologyFunctorIso to get a natural isomorphism from restricted degree-n stalk homology to ambient degree-n stalk homology.

Apply the restricted degree-n stalk homology functor to the square of step 1. Compose its source comparison with the inverse natural isomorphism of step 2, and its inverse target comparison with that natural isomorphism. Naturality and cancellation of the target comparison prove the required conjugacy, implemented by the proved private categorical transportArrow lemma.

lean.statement: theorem standardSingle_open_stalk_arrow {Y B A : Scheme.{u}} (p : Y ⟶ B) [QuasiCompact p] [QuasiSeparated p] (M : Y.Modules) (g : A ⟶ B) (a : A) (S : B.Opens) (V : A.Opens) (hV : a ∈ V) (hVS : V ≤ g ⁻¹ᵁ S) : letI := fun X : Scheme.{u} ↦ HasDerivedCategory.standard (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) let xV : V.toScheme := ⟨a, hV⟩ let F := RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor V.toScheme.toRingedSpace xV ⋙ ModuleCat.restrictScalars (V.stalkIso xV).inv.hom let pS := p ∣_ S let MS := M.restrict (p ⁻¹ᵁ S).ι let j := g.resLE S V hVS ∀ n : ℤ, ∃ (s : (RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor A.toRingedSpace a).obj ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ n).obj ((derivedPullback g).obj ((schemeDerivedDirectImage p).obj ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj M)))) ≅ F.obj ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ n).obj ((derivedPullback j).obj ((schemeDerivedDirectImage pS).obj ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj MS))))) (t : F.obj ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ n).obj ((schemeDerivedDirectImage (pullback.snd pS j)).obj ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullbackObj (pullback.fst pS j) MS)))) ≅ (RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor A.toRingedSpace a).obj ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ n).obj ((schemeDerivedDirectImage (pullback.snd p g)).obj ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullbackObj (pullback.fst p g) M))))), (RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor A.toRingedSpace a).map ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ n).map (standardSingleBaseChangeMap p M g)) = s.hom ≫ F.map ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ n).map (standardSingleBaseChangeMap pS MS j)) ≫ t.hom
